title: Outdoor Unit Configuration Fault
shortDescription: Trane XL/XV outdoor unit cannot load its configuration.
fullDescription:
Code 89.00 on Trane ComfortLink II heat pumps indicates the outdoor control failed to load the unit configuration. This often occurs after a board replacement before the configuration is loaded from the USB stick or ComfortLink thermostat.

Run the Auto-Configure option on the thermostat or load the config file with a service laptop.

fixSteps.title: Auto-configure
fixSteps.instruction: On ComfortLink II thermostat, run Equipment Auto-Configure.

whenToCallPro: Always.

faq.a: The process requires Trane diagnostic procedures, best done by a technician.

title: Outdoor Unit Communication Error
shortDescription: Thermostat cannot reach the outdoor control module.
fullDescription:
Code 89.03 on Trane ComfortLink systems signals loss of communication between the indoor interface and the outdoor control. The system uses a 4-wire RSBus that also provides 24V.

Verify wiring, outdoor power, and terminations.

fixSteps.title: Check power
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm outdoor breaker on.

fixSteps.title: Inspect RSBus
fixSteps.instruction: Verify R, C, Data+ and Data- terminated at both ends.

whenToCallPro: For board issues.

faq.q: Can I use regular thermostat wire?
faq.a: Yes - 18/5 is typical for Trane ComfortLink.

title: Outdoor Unit Internal Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor control board self-test failed.
fullDescription: 89.10 indicates a hardware self-test failure on the outdoor control board. Usually means the board needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut breaker 5 min.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Tech installs new control.

whenToCallPro: Always.

faq.a: Usually $300-$800 plus labor.

title: Outdoor Unit Low Voltage / Power Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor unit detected supply voltage out of range.
fullDescription: 89.20 indicates the outdoor unit's supply voltage is outside the acceptable range (typically 197-253V). Protects the inverter from damage.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Verify L1-L2 at disconnect.

whenToCallPro: If connections are intact but issue persists.

faq.a: Yes - recommended for all inverter heat pumps.

title: Compressor Startup Failure
shortDescription: Compressor failed to start within allowed time.
fullDescription:
91.00 indicates the outdoor compressor did not start successfully. Causes include failed capacitor, stuck compressor, low voltage, or inverter issue.

Check capacitor on non-inverter models first.
safetyWarning: Discharge capacitor before handling.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Open disconnect and discharge cap.

fixSteps.title: Test cap
fixSteps.instruction: Measure uF.

whenToCallPro: For compressor replacement.

faq.q: Can I start it with a hard-start kit?
faq.a: Sometimes, but call a pro to diagnose.

title: Compressor Overcurrent
shortDescription: Compressor drew too much current.
fullDescription: 91.10 indicates the compressor exceeded the overcurrent threshold. Could be high head pressure, weak inverter, or degraded compressor.

fixSteps.title: Clean outdoor
fixSteps.instruction: Rinse condenser.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning doesn't solve it.

faq.a: Protection works but indicates system stress.

title: Discharge Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Compressor discharge temperature sensor failed.
fullDescription:
126.04 indicates the discharge temperature thermistor is open, shorted, or unplugged. Discharge sensing protects the compressor from overheat.

Replace the sensor clipped to the discharge line.

fixSteps.title: Open outdoor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cover.

fixSteps.title: Reseat/replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clip new sensor to discharge line same location.

whenToCallPro: Only if uncomfortable.

faq.a: No - safety shutdown activates.

title: Compressor High Temperature
shortDescription: Compressor discharge temperature too high.
fullDescription: 126.20 means the discharge temperature exceeded the safe maximum (usually 115-120C). Typically caused by low refrigerant, restricted condenser airflow, or a failing EEV.

fixSteps.title: Clean coil
fixSteps.instruction: Rinse condenser fins.

fixSteps.title: Pro diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Charge verification needed.

whenToCallPro: Usually yes.

faq.a: Yes - high discharge temp is a common cause of compressor failure.

title: Reversing Valve Fault
shortDescription: Reversing valve did not shift as expected.
fullDescription: 127.00 indicates the control commanded the reversing valve to switch (e.g., for defrost) but the coil temperature did not change as expected. The valve may be stuck or the solenoid failed.
symptoms: Heat pump stuck in one mode

fixSteps.title: Test solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Measure solenoid coil resistance.

fixSteps.title: Call pro
fixSteps.instruction: Valve replacement requires refrigerant recovery.

whenToCallPro: For valve replacement.

faq.a: Sometimes on a stuck slug; a pro will try this first.

title: Outdoor Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor fan motor not responding.
fullDescription: 161.04 signals the outdoor fan is not operating correctly - stuck, drawing high current, or not reporting RPM (for ECM variable-speed fans). On XV20i systems with ECM outdoor fans, this often points to motor or module failure.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: Spin by hand - should turn freely.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap fan motor assembly.

whenToCallPro: For ECM module issues.

faq.q: Can I use a generic motor?
faq.a: No - ECM motors must match Trane control.

title: Coil Frost Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Defrost/coil temperature sensor reading is invalid.
fullDescription: 174.00 indicates the outdoor coil temperature sensor is open or shorted. Without this sensor defrost logic cannot operate, and the heat pump will shut down or revert to backup heat.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Open disconnect.

fixSteps.title: Reseat/replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clip new 10k thermistor to coil bend.

whenToCallPro: Only if uncomfortable.

faq.a: Often yes - this is mostly a heating concern.

title: EEV (Electronic Expansion Valve) Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor EEV not responding correctly.
fullDescription: 175.20 indicates the outdoor electronic expansion valve is not moving as commanded or its feedback is lost. Often a stuck EEV motor or a disconnected wiring harness.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect outdoor.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat 4-6 wire connector on EEV coil.

whenToCallPro: For EEV replacement (involves refrigerant recovery).

faq.a: It meters refrigerant like a TXV but is controlled electronically.

title: Outdoor Fan Motor Locked Rotor
shortDescription: Outdoor fan motor cannot start or has stalled.
fullDescription: Trane code 89.30 indicates the outdoor unit's variable-speed fan motor reports a locked rotor condition. The unit will retry several times before locking out the cooling/heating cycle.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening control panels. High-voltage capacitors can hold a lethal charge even after power is removed.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect and Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the disconnect, remove top grille, and clear any debris around the fan blade.

fixSteps.title: Spin the Blade
fixSteps.instruction: Manually rotate the blade - it should turn freely with minimal resistance.

fixSteps.title: Test Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: On PSC motors, measure the run capacitor.

whenToCallPro: If the blade is seized or the motor fails to spin freely, call a pro.

faq.q: Can debris really stop the motor?
faq.a: Yes - leaves, twigs, or ice in the fan can prevent startup torque.

title: Reversing Valve Stuck
shortDescription: Heat pump cannot switch between heating and cooling.
fullDescription: Trane 90.10 indicates the system commanded a reversing valve change but did not detect the corresponding pressure shift. The valve may be mechanically stuck.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.

causes.cause: Low refrigerant charge preventing valve shift

symptoms: Stuck in heat or stuck in cool

fixSteps.title: Tap the Valve
fixSteps.instruction: With caution and power off, lightly tap the reversing valve body during a transition - sometimes frees a stuck pilot.

fixSteps.title: Test Solenoid Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance on the reversing valve coil.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant-side work and valve replacement are professional jobs.

faq.q: Will it cool but not heat?
faq.a: Often yes - valves often fail in the de-energized (cool) position.

title: Compressor Overcurrent
shortDescription: Compressor drew current above safe threshold.
fullDescription: Trane code 93.00 means the inverter or contactor sensed compressor amp draw above the rated trip threshold. The unit shuts down to protect the compressor.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.

fixSteps.title: Wash Condenser Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Spray the outdoor coil from the inside out with a garden hose to remove buildup.

fixSteps.title: Verify Clearances
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure 24 inches of clearance around the unit.

fixSteps.title: Pro Charge Check
fixSteps.instruction: A technician must verify subcooling and superheat to confirm proper charge.

whenToCallPro: Compressor faults need a refrigeration tech.

faq.a: Repeated trips can - resolve the underlying cause quickly.

title: Compressor Lockout - High Pressure
shortDescription: High-pressure switch tripped 5 times.
fullDescription: Trane 105.00 represents a hard lockout after the high-pressure switch in the discharge line opened multiple times within the same cycle window.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.

fixSteps.title: Clean Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Wash outdoor coil thoroughly.

fixSteps.title: Verify Fan Operation
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm condenser fan runs whenever the compressor runs.

fixSteps.title: Pro Recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Tech may need to recover and recharge with proper subcooling.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning does not restore operation, professional refrigerant work is needed.

faq.q: Why does it lock out after 5 trips?
faq.a: To prevent damage from repeated high-pressure events.

title: Compressor Lockout - Low Pressure
shortDescription: Low-pressure switch tripped 5 times.
fullDescription: Trane 110.00 indicates a hard lockout after the suction-side low-pressure switch repeatedly opened, signaling refrigerant starvation.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.

causes.cause: Stuck TXV or restricted metering device

symptoms: Ice on outdoor or indoor coil

fixSteps.title: Replace Filter, Run Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Run blower for 2 hours to thaw any frozen coil.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for Frost
fixSteps.instruction: Check both coils for frost or ice.

fixSteps.title: Pro Leak Search
fixSteps.instruction: A technician must use electronic leak detector or UV dye to locate the leak.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant leaks must be repaired by a certified tech.

faq.a: No - EPA Section 608 certification is required.

title: Defrost Termination Fault
shortDescription: Heat pump did not exit defrost properly.
fullDescription: Trane code 125.00 means a defrost cycle ran longer than the maximum allowed time without the coil reaching the termination temperature.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.

fixSteps.title: Test Coil Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance vs. ambient temperature using the spec chart.

fixSteps.title: Pro Diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: If sensor is good, refrigerant pressures and reversing valve must be checked.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant or reversing valve issues need a technician.

faq.a: Typically 2-10 minutes; over 12 minutes is a fault.

title: Discharge Line Temperature High
shortDescription: Compressor discharge thermistor sensed unsafe temperature.
fullDescription: Trane 145.00 indicates the compressor discharge line temperature exceeded the safe threshold (typically 240F+). The control shuts down to prevent oil breakdown and compressor damage.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.

fixSteps.title: Clean Outdoor Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Wash and verify clearances.

fixSteps.title: Pro Charge & Sensor Test
fixSteps.instruction: Tech should verify charge by superheat and replace the discharge thermistor if reading abnormally high.

whenToCallPro: Always pro - high discharge temp risks compressor failure.

faq.q: Can I run the unit with this fault?
faq.a: No - extended high-temp operation will damage the compressor.

title: Inverter Drive Over Temperature
shortDescription: Variable-speed inverter exceeded thermal limit.
fullDescription: Trane code 150.00 (XV20i and similar) means the outdoor inverter drive heatsink exceeded its thermal cutoff. The drive will derate or shut down until cool.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening control panels. High-voltage capacitors can hold a lethal charge even after power is removed.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Drive Cooling
fixSteps.instruction: Open the control compartment (power off!) and check for debris on the drive heatsink.

fixSteps.title: Verify Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for the inverter cooling fan during a cycle.

whenToCallPro: Drive replacement requires Trane-trained technician.

faq.a: The inverter dissipates significant heat - any cooling failure quickly causes thermal trips.

title: Outdoor Air Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor temperature sensor open or short.
fullDescription: Trane 180.00 indicates the outdoor air temperature thermistor is reading out of range. The control loses input needed for defrost timing and capacity staging.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening control panels. High-voltage capacitors can hold a lethal charge even after power is removed.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Re-seat the sensor plug at the outdoor control board.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Compare resistance to spec chart at known temperature.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clip the new thermistor in the same airflow location.

whenToCallPro: If sensor and wiring check good, a pro should test the board input.

faq.a: Often yes, but defrost cycles may run too often or too rarely.

title: Communication Loss - XL Series
shortDescription: ComfortLink II network communication lost.
fullDescription: Trane code 200.00 indicates the indoor unit, outdoor unit, or thermostat has dropped off the ComfortLink II communication bus.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening control panels. High-voltage capacitors can hold a lethal charge even after power is removed.

causes.cause: Bus wire damaged by rodents or weather

symptoms: System falls back to non-comm mode

fixSteps.title: Re-seat Terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten the four bus terminals at thermostat, indoor unit, and outdoor unit.

fixSteps.title: Verify Polarity
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm color-to-letter mapping matches at all three locations.

fixSteps.title: Wire Continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Run continuity end-to-end on each conductor.

whenToCallPro: If wiring checks good, a Trane technician with ComfortLink II tools is needed.

faq.a: ComfortLink II uses dedicated comm pairs to carry digital data alongside power.

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Open
shortDescription: Outdoor coil thermistor open circuit.
fullDescription: Trane diagnostic 211.00 indicates the outdoor coil temperature sensor is open. Defrost cycle logic and refrigerant protection cannot run.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate clip on outdoor coil and reseat.

fixSteps.title: Test Continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance — should be in 10kΩ range.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Snap-in clip; route wires safely.

whenToCallPro: If wiring tests fine and resistance is correct, suspect the defrost board.

faq.a: Mostly affects heating defrost; cooling continues with reduced protection.

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Shorted
shortDescription: Outdoor coil thermistor reads short.
fullDescription: 211.10 is the shorted version of the coil sensor fault — resistance reads near zero.

fixSteps.title: Check Routing
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect harness for damage where it contacts sheet metal.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm sensor is shorted vs harness is the issue.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Install new clip-on thermistor.

whenToCallPro: If you cannot find a wiring fault.

faq.q: Why does shorted vs open matter?
faq.a: Different fault codes help techs diagnose faster.

title: Suction Pressure Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Suction transducer reading invalid.
fullDescription: 212.00 indicates the suction pressure transducer on variable-capacity Trane heat pumps is sending invalid voltage to the board.
symptoms: Variable-speed unit drops to fixed speed

fixSteps.title: Inspect Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Locate Schrader-mount transducer; check 5V harness.

fixSteps.title: Replace Transducer
fixSteps.instruction: Schrader-style — quick swap with minimal refrigerant loss.

whenToCallPro: Always — Schrader removal still requires care.

faq.a: A few oz at most when removing Schrader-style transducers.

safetyWarning: Pressurized refrigerant — eye protection mandatory.

title: EXV Position Error
shortDescription: Electronic expansion valve out of step.
fullDescription: 215.00 is reported when the EXV motor steps don't track the commanded position — usually a stalled valve or driver fault.

fixSteps.title: Reset Steps
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle to re-home the EXV.

fixSteps.title: Test Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Measure EXV coil windings (typically ~50Ω).

fixSteps.title: Replace EXV
fixSteps.instruction: Sealed-system work to swap valve body.

whenToCallPro: Always — EXV replacement is a sealed-system repair.

faq.a: Sometimes — power cycle re-homes the valve and resolves transient issues.

title: Reversing Valve Failure
shortDescription: Reversing valve did not shift on command.
fullDescription: 224.00 indicates the indoor and outdoor coil temps did not change as expected after the board energized the reversing valve. The valve is stuck.
symptoms: Valve hisses but no mode change

fixSteps.title: Tap Valve
fixSteps.instruction: With the call active, gently tap the valve body to shift slide.

fixSteps.title: Replace Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Slip-off solenoid coil swap.

fixSteps.title: Replace Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Recovery + brazing if valve body itself fails.

whenToCallPro: If tapping and coil replacement don't help, the valve body must come out.

faq.q: Why a heat pump and not AC?
faq.a: Heat pumps reverse the cycle; AC-only units don't have this valve.

title: Defrost Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Defrost initiate sensor invalid.
fullDescription: 240.00 is set when the defrost-initiate thermistor fails. Without this sensor the heat pump cannot decide when to defrost.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Pull and reseat with dielectric grease.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Match resistance against ambient temp chart.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clip-on swap.

whenToCallPro: If sensor and wiring are OK, defrost board may be at fault.

faq.a: Some Trane boards have a defrost initiate button for testing.

title: Outdoor Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor fan motor not responding.
fullDescription: 260.00 indicates the outdoor fan motor (typically ECM) is not running at commanded speed.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; check for binding.

fixSteps.title: Test Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: PSC fans only.

fixSteps.title: Module Swap
fixSteps.instruction: ECM models: replace end-bell module.

whenToCallPro: ECM motors require Trane-spec replacement.

faq.a: Pressure protection trips when condenser fan stops.

title: Defrost Termination Failed
shortDescription: Defrost cycle exceeded max time.
fullDescription: 286.00 indicates the unit entered defrost but coil temperature did not climb to terminate-temperature within the maximum allowed time.

fixSteps.title: Verify Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Check defrost sensor reading vs actual coil temp.

fixSteps.title: Pro Charge Check
fixSteps.instruction: Tech verifies refrigerant charge.

fixSteps.title: Address Reversing Valve
fixSteps.instruction: If valve partially shifts, replace.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant work always pro.

faq.a: Aux electric heat will engage during defrost — bills go up.

title: Compressor Discharge Temp High
shortDescription: Compressor discharge thermistor over limit.
fullDescription: 320.00 fires when discharge temp exceeds safe operating limit. Compressor lockout follows.

fixSteps.title: Cool Down
fixSteps.instruction: Allow 30 min cool-down.

fixSteps.title: Pro Diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Superheat / subcool analysis.

whenToCallPro: Discharge temp issues are charge-related.

faq.a: If recurring, oil breakdown shortens compressor life.

title: Indoor/Outdoor Mismatch
shortDescription: Indoor and outdoor units don't match.
fullDescription: 400.00 is reported when the indoor (TAM) and outdoor (TWE/4TWR) communicating units are mismatched in capacity or model series.

causes.cause: Wrong indoor coil with new outdoor

symptoms: Unit refuses to start after install

fixSteps.title: Check Model Numbers
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm indoor/outdoor compatibility per Trane match-up guide.

fixSteps.title: Set Configuration
fixSteps.instruction: Use ComfortLink II / installer menu to set correct indoor model.

fixSteps.title: Replace Mismatched Coil
fixSteps.instruction: If truly mismatched, only fix is correct coil.

whenToCallPro: Always — mismatched systems must be matched per OEM tables.

faq.a: Only if Trane published a match — otherwise warranty void and efficiency suffers.

title: 130.00 — Outdoor Fan Failure
shortDescription: Outdoor fan motor not running during compressor call.
fullDescription: Trane CleanEffects/XV20i diagnostic 130.00 indicates the outdoor fan ECM is not producing tach feedback within 30 seconds of compressor start. Without airflow, high-pressure trip will follow shortly.

fixSteps.title: Confirm visually
fixSteps.instruction: Open top grille, fan should spin during compressor call.

fixSteps.title: Reseat motor plug
fixSteps.instruction: 5-pin Molex at motor.

fixSteps.title: Replace ECM
fixSteps.instruction: Trane MOT18811.

whenToCallPro: ECM replacement requires programming via service tool.

faq.a: No — compressor will trip on high pressure within 1 minute.

title: 131.10 — Outdoor Fan Locked Rotor
shortDescription: ECM reported locked rotor condition.
fullDescription: Code 131.10 fires when the ECM outdoor fan attempts start but cannot turn — most often due to ice or debris in the blade path.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Breaker off, lock out.

fixSteps.title: Clear blades
fixSteps.instruction: Remove debris; thaw ice with warm (not boiling) water.

fixSteps.title: Free spin test
fixSteps.instruction: By hand, no resistance acceptable.

whenToCallPro: If bearings damaged, motor replacement needed.

faq.q: How does ice get on a heat pump fan?
faq.a: Failed defrost cycle - water from melt re-froze. Address defrost issue too.

safetyWarning: Cut power before clearing — fan may suddenly free and start.

title: 180.10 — Compressor Discharge Temperature High
shortDescription: Compressor discharge thermistor exceeded 250F.
fullDescription: 180.10 protects the compressor: discharge gas temp above 250F indicates low charge, dirty filter, or failed TXV. Compressor stops until temp drops below 200F.

fixSteps.title: Filter check
fixSteps.instruction: Replace; verify all registers open.

fixSteps.title: Subcool measurement
fixSteps.instruction: Tech verify charge per nameplate.

fixSteps.title: TXV diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: If subcool normal but superheat high, TXV stuck closed.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant work requires EPA certification.

faq.a: Only EPA-licensed techs may handle refrigerants.

title: 198.10 — Compressor Crankcase Heater Open
shortDescription: Crankcase heater current draw zero when expected.
fullDescription: Trane variable-speed XV20i monitors crankcase heater current. 198.10 indicates open heater circuit — risk of compressor flood-back on next cold start.

fixSteps.title: Continuity test
fixSteps.instruction: Heater should ohm 50-200 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Replace heater
fixSteps.instruction: Belly band heater wraps compressor.

fixSteps.title: Verify relay
fixSteps.instruction: If new heater also doesn't draw, relay on board failed.

whenToCallPro: Relay failures require board replacement.

faq.a: Without crankcase heat, refrigerant collects in compressor sump as liquid - damages on next start.

title: 212.10 — Liquid Line Solenoid Valve Failure
shortDescription: Solenoid not energizing or stuck.
fullDescription: On Trane heat pumps with liquid-line shutoff solenoid, 212.10 means solenoid commanded but coil current incorrect. Could be open coil, failed driver, or stuck plunger.

fixSteps.title: Coil resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Should read 200-400 ohms across coil.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Slides off stem - inexpensive.

fixSteps.title: Valve body service
fixSteps.instruction: If stuck, recovery + replacement needed.

whenToCallPro: Valve body replacement requires brazing.

faq.q: Do all heat pumps have this?
faq.a: No - only systems with pump-down or dual-fuel hybrid setups.

title: 260.10 — Charge Loss Detected (Algorithm)
shortDescription: Performance algorithm detected charge below 80% of nameplate.
fullDescription: Trane CommunicaTRANE units calculate charge from delta-T, pressure, and current readings. 260.10 fires when sustained data suggests low charge before pressure switches trip.

fixSteps.title: Visual inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Check Schraders, service ports, evap connections for oil.

fixSteps.title: Electronic leak detection
fixSteps.instruction: Tech to sweep system.

fixSteps.title: Repair and recharge
fixSteps.instruction: Per nameplate.

whenToCallPro: Charge work always requires certified tech.

faq.q: How quickly will it fail completely?
faq.a: Depends on leak rate - days to months.

title: 310.00 — Outdoor Coil Sensor Drift
shortDescription: Outdoor coil sensor reading drifts vs. ambient.
fullDescription: 310.00 is a soft fault — outdoor coil sensor reading inconsistent with ambient. Most often a strap that came loose or sensor in direct sunlight.

fixSteps.title: Re-strap sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Coil clip on lower return bend, away from sun.

fixSteps.title: Replace if needed
fixSteps.instruction: Trane SEN01184.

whenToCallPro: If wires routed inside cabinet badly, defer to tech.

faq.a: Soft warning - system runs, defrost timing affected.

title: 410.10 — Outdoor Air Sensor Failure
shortDescription: Outdoor ambient sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription: 410.10 means the outdoor air thermistor used for balance point and demand defrost is reading invalid. System reverts to fixed time/temp defrost and disables economizer logic.
symptoms: Aux heat runs at higher temps

fixSteps.title: Inspect mounting
fixSteps.instruction: On outdoor cabinet, shielded from sun.

fixSteps.title: Resistance check
fixSteps.instruction: 10k at 25C nominal.

whenToCallPro: Internal cabinet routing may need tech.

faq.a: Yes - with reduced efficiency.

title: 420.10 — Variable Speed Drive Bus Capacitor Aging
shortDescription: DC bus ripple voltage exceeded threshold — capacitors aging.
fullDescription: Inverter drives in Trane XV20i monitor DC bus capacitor health by ripple voltage. 420.10 is a predictive warning: capacitors at end-of-life within ~6 months. Drive still works but should be scheduled for replacement.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Drive replacement is planned, not emergency.

fixSteps.title: Improve ventilation
fixSteps.instruction: Clear vents around drive housing if blocked.

fixSteps.title: Drive swap
fixSteps.instruction: Trane CTL01023 typical.

whenToCallPro: Drive replacement requires Trane training and re-pairing.

faq.a: Yes, for several months - but plan replacement.

safetyWarning: DC bus stays charged 5+ minutes after power off.

title: 520.10 — Indoor Communication Lost
shortDescription: Variable-speed outdoor unit lost RS-485 to indoor air handler.
fullDescription: 520.10 fires when the outdoor inverter board loses comm with the indoor variable-speed blower. Without comm, both units fall back to default fixed-speed operation.

fixSteps.title: Reseat comm wires
fixSteps.instruction: i+/i- terminals at both indoor and outdoor.

fixSteps.title: Verify routing
fixSteps.instruction: 6 inch separation from line voltage cables.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: 60-second breaker cycle to reset both boards.

whenToCallPro: Board replacement requires Trane service tool.

faq.q: Can I use generic thermostat wire?
faq.a: Short runs OK — long runs require shielded twisted pair per Trane spec.

title: Trane code 1
shortDescription: Trane heat-pump code 1 fault.
fullDescription: Trane heat-pump code 1 fault. Common Trane fault.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Check.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Replace.

whenToCallPro: Contact service.

faq.a: Resolve before use.

title: Trane code 2
shortDescription: Trane heat-pump code 2 fault.
fullDescription: Trane heat-pump code 2 fault. Common Trane fault.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Check.

title: Low Compressor Load — Mass Flow Below Threshold
shortDescription: The compressor is drawing significantly less current than expected.
fullDescription: Trane Comfortlink II heat pumps post code 16 when the outdoor compressor current sensor reports load substantially below the model's expected value at the commanded stage. Common in low ambient with low refrigerant charge, or when the reversing valve is partially stuck. The system stages back and posts the warning rather than locking out.
safetyWarning: Electrical safety: turn off the disconnect and the breaker before removing service panels. Capacitors can hold a lethal charge — discharge before touching terminals. Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Carbon monoxide detectors must be installed when servicing gas-fired equipment.

causes.cause: Faulty current transformer on the compressor leg

symptoms: Reduced heating capacity — long run times
Code 16 in the Comfortlink II diagnostics

fixSteps.title: Check Air Filter and Coils
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the indoor filter and brush off the outdoor coil to rule out airflow issues.

fixSteps.title: Read Diagnostics
fixSteps.instruction: From the iComfort or Comfortlink thermostat, record stored fault codes and operating data.

fixSteps.title: Refrigerant Service
fixSteps.instruction: An EPA-certified technician should weigh-in or top-off charge per Trane's superheat/subcool tables.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant work and reversing valve service require EPA Section 608 certification.

faq.q: Can low load damage the compressor?
faq.a: Long-term operation with low charge causes overheating and oil dilution; do not run for weeks unaddressed.
No — it stages the unit back and continues running, but it should be diagnosed promptly.

title: High Pressure Switch Open
shortDescription: The discharge-side high-pressure cutout has tripped, locking out the compressor.
fullDescription: Trane heat pumps include a high-pressure switch on the discharge line that opens at approximately 600 psi (R-410A). Code 26 means the switch tripped — usually from restricted condenser airflow, refrigerant overcharge, or a non-condensable in the system. Three trips in 60 minutes places the unit in hard lockout requiring manual reset.
safetyWarning: Electrical safety: turn off the disconnect and the breaker before removing service panels. Capacitors can hold a lethal charge — discharge before touching terminals. Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Carbon monoxide detectors must be installed when servicing gas-fired equipment.

causes.cause: Dirty or restricted outdoor condenser coil
Outdoor fan motor or capacitor failure
Indoor coil iced or blocked in heat mode
Bad reversing valve in cooling causing high head

symptoms: Compressor stops after a short run
Discharge line very hot before shutdown

fixSteps.title: Clean Condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, then rinse the outdoor coil with low-pressure water from the inside out.

fixSteps.title: Verify Outdoor Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the fan ramps up under cooling/heating; replace failed fan capacitor if needed.

fixSteps.title: Check Charge
fixSteps.instruction: An EPA-certified tech should verify subcool/superheat against Trane's chart.

whenToCallPro: Anytime gauges go on the system or the compressor is suspect.

faq.q: Why does the high-pressure switch trip?
faq.a: Anything that prevents heat from leaving the condenser raises pressure: dirty coils, dead fans, overcharge, blocked airflow.
Never — it protects the compressor from catastrophic failure.

title: Defrost Cycle Duration Exceeded
shortDescription: A defrost cycle ran longer than the maximum allowed time without satisfying the termination sensor.
fullDescription: Code 31 is set when the heat pump entered defrost (running the compressor in cooling with the outdoor fan off) and the outdoor coil sensor never reached the termination temperature within the maximum 10-minute window. The control aborts defrost, posts code 31, and resumes heating. Repeated 31 codes mean the defrost sensor or reversing valve is suspect.
safetyWarning: Electrical safety: turn off the disconnect and the breaker before removing service panels. Capacitors can hold a lethal charge — discharge before touching terminals. Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Carbon monoxide detectors must be installed when servicing gas-fired equipment.

causes.cause: Reversing valve not shifting fully into cooling
Low refrigerant charge limiting heat to the outdoor coil
Severe ice load from defrost intervals set too long
Outdoor fan stuck on during defrost

symptoms: Heavy ice on the outdoor coil
Reduced heating capacity in cold weather

fixSteps.title: Adjust Defrost Interval
fixSteps.instruction: Set the defrost interval to 30 or 60 minutes (depending on climate) using the Comfortlink service screens.

fixSteps.title: Test Coil Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, measure the outdoor coil sensor; typical 10 kΩ at 25 °C thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Check Reversing Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for the valve solenoid energizing during defrost; replace the solenoid coil if dead.

whenToCallPro: If the reversing valve or refrigerant charge is suspect.

faq.q: Why is my coil iced over?
faq.a: Defrost is failing to clear ice. Continued operation can damage the outdoor fan blade striking ice — turn off the heat pump and run on auxiliary heat until repaired.

faq.q: Can I run on emergency heat?
faq.a: Yes — set the thermostat to Em Heat to bypass the heat pump and run only the auxiliary strips or furnace.

title: Compressor Did Not Start
shortDescription: The control commanded the compressor on but no current was sensed.
fullDescription: Trane Comfortlink II reports code 33 when the contactor was energized but the compressor current transformer reads zero. The compressor either failed to start (open windings, locked rotor, bad capacitor) or the contactor never closed. Three failures lock the unit out for 60 minutes.
safetyWarning: Electrical safety: turn off the disconnect and the breaker before removing service panels. Capacitors can hold a lethal charge — discharge before touching terminals. Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Carbon monoxide detectors must be installed when servicing gas-fired equipment.

causes.cause: Failed run capacitor on single-phase units

symptoms: Outdoor fan may run but compressor is silent

fixSteps.title: Listen and Look
fixSteps.instruction: Watch for fan-only or hum-and-trip behavior at the outdoor unit.

fixSteps.title: Test Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: With power off and capacitor discharged, measure the run capacitor against its rated µF.

fixSteps.title: Test Compressor Windings
fixSteps.instruction: An EPA-certified tech should measure C-S, C-R, and S-R resistance and confirm to ground continuity.

whenToCallPro: Compressor electrical diagnosis and replacement are professional repairs.

faq.q: Can I just replace the capacitor?
faq.a: Often yes — a failed run capacitor is the most common cause. If the compressor still won't start with a good cap, deeper diagnosis is needed.

faq.q: How long does a compressor last?
faq.a: Trane scrolls typically last 12-15 years. Beyond that, replacement of the entire condensing unit may be more economical.

title: Defrost Termination Sensor Failure
shortDescription: The outdoor coil temperature sensor reads open, shorted, or out of range.
fullDescription: Code 41 indicates the defrost termination thermistor is reporting an invalid resistance — typically below 100 Ω (shorted) or above 100 kΩ (open). Without this sensor the control falls back to time-only defrost, which may over-defrost or under-defrost.
safetyWarning: Electrical safety: turn off the disconnect and the breaker before removing service panels. Capacitors can hold a lethal charge — discharge before touching terminals. Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Carbon monoxide detectors must be installed when servicing gas-fired equipment.

causes.cause: Cracked thermistor housing letting water in
Loose connection at the outdoor control board

symptoms: Heavy ice on outdoor coil or excessive defrost cycles

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open the outdoor control compartment and reseat the sensor connector.

fixSteps.title: Measure Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, measure resistance — typical 10 kΩ near freezing. Replace if open or shorted.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wire Run
fixSteps.instruction: Look for chafing where the cable enters the cabinet; replace the sensor assembly if damaged.

whenToCallPro: If the control board's sensor input has failed.

faq.q: Will the heat pump still work?
faq.a: Yes — the control reverts to time-only defrost. It is less efficient but functional.
Trane defrost thermistors typically cost $25-60 USD, plus labor.

title: No Auxiliary Flame on Heat Call
shortDescription: The auxiliary furnace did not light when called by the heat pump's defrost or backup logic.
fullDescription: On dual-fuel installations Trane heat pumps call the auxiliary furnace whenever defrost runs or when outdoor temperature falls below the balance point. Code 79 indicates the heat pump received no flame confirmation from the furnace within the expected timeframe — usually a furnace-side issue rather than a heat-pump fault.
safetyWarning: Gas appliance safety: if you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas utility from outside. Do not operate switches, phones, or appliances. Shut off the gas at the manual valve before any service. Combustion work should be performed by a licensed HVAC technician; improper repair can cause carbon monoxide poisoning, fire, or explosion.

causes.cause: Furnace ignition fault (see furnace fault codes)
Closed manual gas valve to the furnace
Loose W2 wire between thermostat and furnace
Faulty flame proving feedback to Comfortlink

symptoms: Heat pump posts code 79 during defrost
Furnace simultaneously shows its own ignition fault
House fails to recover from setbacks

fixSteps.title: Check Furnace Fault
fixSteps.instruction: Read the furnace's own LED fault code first — fix it before troubleshooting the heat pump.

fixSteps.title: Verify Gas Supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the manual gas valve is fully open.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Thermostat Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Verify W2 (or aux) is connected between thermostat, furnace, and heat pump board.

whenToCallPro: If the furnace itself is faulty — repair the furnace per its manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: Is this a heat-pump or furnace problem?
faq.a: Almost always a furnace problem. Diagnose the furnace first.

faq.q: Will the heat pump still run?
faq.a: Yes — heat-pump heating continues, but defrosts will be cold without auxiliary heat.

title: Gas Valve Solenoid Output Fault
shortDescription: The integrated furnace control reports a fault on the gas valve drive output.
fullDescription: On Trane gas/heat-pump dual-fuel systems the integrated furnace control board reports code 89 when the microprocessor detects an issue with the gas valve driver — either the relay output is not switching or the valve is drawing abnormal current. Combustion is locked out until the fault is cleared.
safetyWarning: Gas appliance safety: if you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas utility from outside. Do not operate switches, phones, or appliances. Shut off the gas at the manual valve before any service. Combustion work should be performed by a licensed HVAC technician; improper repair can cause carbon monoxide poisoning, fire, or explosion.

causes.cause: Damaged wiring harness from board to valve
Failed gas-valve driver on the control board
Reverse-polarity 24 V wiring on the gas valve

symptoms: No gas hiss during ignition sequence

fixSteps.title: Verify Manual Gas Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the upstream manual gas valve is open.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the gas-valve harness on both ends and look for chafing.

fixSteps.title: Replace Gas Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Gas valve replacement requires a licensed HVAC technician with leak-test equipment.

whenToCallPro: Always — gas-valve work requires a licensed technician.

faq.q: Can I run heat pump only?
faq.a: Yes, but the system will be cold during defrost without auxiliary heat in cold weather.

faq.q: How much is a gas valve?
faq.a: $150-300 for the part, $300-700 installed including leak-testing.

title: Loss of Power to Outdoor Unit
shortDescription: The indoor air handler cannot communicate with or detect the outdoor unit.
fullDescription: Code 95 means the indoor unit's communication or 24 V Y signal to the outdoor heat pump is reaching nothing — either the outdoor unit has lost 240 V supply or the communication wires have failed. The system reverts to auxiliary heat only.
safetyWarning: Electrical safety: turn off the disconnect and the breaker before removing service panels. Capacitors can hold a lethal charge — discharge before touching terminals. Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Carbon monoxide detectors must be installed when servicing gas-fired equipment.

causes.cause: Blown 5 A fuse on the outdoor low-voltage circuit

fixSteps.title: Check Disconnect
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the outdoor disconnect handle and confirm the breaker has not tripped.

fixSteps.title: Test 240 V at Disconnect
fixSteps.instruction: With service-rated tester, confirm 240 V at the line side of the disconnect.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Communication Wire
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the thermostat wire from indoor to outdoor; replace if damaged.

whenToCallPro: If the breaker keeps tripping or the outdoor control board has failed.

faq.a: Locked compressor, shorted contactor coil, or chewed wire to ground. Investigate before resetting.
Yes — rodents commonly chew low-voltage wiring outside; protect with conduit or rodent guards.

title: Outdoor Unit Liquid-Line Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The liquid-line temperature sensor on the outdoor coil is reporting out-of-range values.
fullDescription: Trane Comfortlink II uses a liquid-line thermistor for charge verification and defrost-termination logic. Code 126 indicates the sensor is open or shorted. The unit can still run but charge balancing and Comfortlink charge-verify functions are disabled.
safetyWarning: Electrical safety: turn off the disconnect and the breaker before removing service panels. Capacitors can hold a lethal charge — discharge before touching terminals. Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Carbon monoxide detectors must be installed when servicing gas-fired equipment.

causes.cause: Loose connector at the outdoor control board
Failed sensor input on outdoor control board

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open the outdoor control box and firmly reseat the liquid-line sensor connector.

fixSteps.title: Measure Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, measure the thermistor at ambient — replace if open or shorted.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a Trane-spec liquid-line thermistor; route away from sharp metal edges.

whenToCallPro: If the outdoor control-board input has failed.

faq.a: Slightly — the unit cannot trim charge or defrost as precisely. Heat output stays mostly normal.

faq.q: How long does this sensor last?
faq.a: Typically 8-12 years. Earlier failures usually trace to physical damage or moisture intrusion.

title: Outdoor Air Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The outdoor ambient temperature sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription: Code 127 reports the outdoor air temperature thermistor is out of range. Comfortlink uses this sensor for balance-point logic, defrost interval selection, and electric-heat staging. Without it the system uses default fallback values, which may run aux heat earlier than necessary.
safetyWarning: Electrical safety: turn off the disconnect and the breaker before removing service panels. Capacitors can hold a lethal charge — discharge before touching terminals. Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Carbon monoxide detectors must be installed when servicing gas-fired equipment.

causes.cause: Mounted in direct sunlight reading falsely high

symptoms: Auxiliary heat may run more than expected

fixSteps.title: Inspect Mounting
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the sensor is mounted on a shaded surface of the outdoor cabinet.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open the control box and reseat the sensor harness.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new Trane outdoor air thermistor with strain relief.

whenToCallPro: If the wiring is damaged inside the cabinet or the control board input is failed.

faq.a: No — it is a control-optimization sensor. The system runs but is less efficient.
If you are comfortable with low-voltage wiring and the unit is powered off at the disconnect, yes.
